subject: english-language-arts
title: Launch and diagnostic: determining where a text leaves matters uncertain
focus: determining where a text leaves matters uncertain
essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to determining where a text leaves matters uncertain change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what determining where a text leaves matters uncertain means in this unit and why it changes an interpretation or a draft.

Apply determining where a text leaves matters uncertain to text at the level described for this course: in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range.
Judge the sufficiency of the learner's own evidence about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain and revise using stated criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
The learner gives cited textual evidence and reasoning rather than an unsupported assertion.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name the next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
assigned text from the course text bank, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on determining where a text leaves matters uncertain. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Model the move on a text that resists a first reading. Show where a competent reader slows down, backtracks, or suspends judgment. Keep the explanation centered on determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.

Work one example together on genuinely difficult material, with an annotated exemplar available for reference. Require the learner to state what the exemplar does not settle. The object of practice is determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.

The learner completes a new application on 11-CCR material, may consult the annotated exemplar, and must record where the text left matters uncertain. The learner writes this response; the tutor may question or critique but may not draft it.
In one concise response, state the most important claim about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application on 11-CCR material, may consult the annotated exemplar, and must record where the text left matters uncertain. Focus: determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
formative_check: State the most important claim about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain and identify one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for determining where a text leaves matters uncertain, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for determining where a text leaves matters uncertain works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar 11-CCR text and state explicitly which conclusions the evidence does not support.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of determining where a text leaves matters uncertain in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to audience values and possible biases change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what audience values and possible biases means in this unit and why it changes an interpretation or a draft.
Apply audience values and possible biases to text at the level described for this course: in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range.
Judge the sufficiency of the learner's own evidence about audience values and possible biases and revise using stated criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about audience values and possible biases.
The learner gives cited textual evidence and reasoning rather than an unsupported assertion.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name the next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
assigned text from the course text bank, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on audience values and possible biases. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Model the move on a text that resists a first reading. Show where a competent reader slows down, backtracks, or suspends judgment. Keep the explanation centered on audience values and possible biases.

Work one example together on genuinely difficult material, with an annotated exemplar available for reference. Require the learner to state what the exemplar does not settle. The object of practice is audience values and possible biases.

The learner completes a new application on 11-CCR material, may consult the annotated exemplar, and must record where the text left matters uncertain. The learner writes this response; the tutor may question or critique but may not draft it.
In one concise response, state the most important claim about audience values and possible biases and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application on 11-CCR material, may consult the annotated exemplar, and must record where the text left matters uncertain. Focus: audience values and possible biases.
formative_check: State the most important claim about audience values and possible biases and identify one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for audience values and possible biases, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for audience values and possible biases works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about audience values and possible biases, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of audience values and possible biases.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar 11-CCR text and state explicitly which conclusions the evidence does not support.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting audience values and possible biases.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
